# Course Schedule

Still in active development.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| output: asis

import re
import html
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import date, timedelta

FIRST_MEETING = date(2026, 9, 14)  # Mon — course_design/syllabus.md: Fall 2026, MWF


def read_var(name, path=Path("_variables.yml")):
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return ""
    m = re.search(rf'^{re.escape(name)}:\s*"(.*?)"\s*$', text, re.MULTILINE)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


NOTEBOOK_BASE = read_var("notebook_base")
NOTEBOOK_HOVER = read_var("example_hover") or "Opens in Google Colab"

LESSON_EMOJI = "📖"
PREP_EMOJI = "🌱"
SLIDES_EMOJI = "🧑‍🏫"
NOTEBOOK_EMOJI = "📓"
PRACTICE_EMOJI = "🏃‍♂️‍➡️"

FRONTMATTER_RE = re.compile(r"^---\s*\n(.*?)\n---", re.DOTALL)
TITLE_RE = re.compile(r'^title:\s*"?(.*?)"?\s*$', re.MULTILINE)


def get_title(path: Path, fallback: str) -> str:
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return fallback
    fm = FRONTMATTER_RE.match(text)
    if not fm:
        return fallback
    m = TITLE_RE.search(fm.group(1))
    if not m:
        return fallback
    title = m.group(1).strip().replace('\\"', '"')
    return title or fallback


def exists_nonempty(p: Path) -> bool:
    return p.is_file() and p.stat().st_size > 0


def collect(folder: str, type_name: str, ext: str):
    """Map (unit, day) -> list of (suffix_or_None, path) for every matching,
    non-empty file. Accepts an optional trailing _<suffix> so a day can have
    more than one file of the same kind (e.g. notebook1_1_example.ipynb)."""
    pattern = re.compile(rf"^{type_name}(\d+)_(\d+)(?:_([A-Za-z0-9-]+))?\.{ext}$")
    out = {}
    d = Path(folder)
    if not d.is_dir():
        return out
    for p in sorted(d.glob(f"*.{ext}")):
        m = pattern.match(p.name)
        if not m or not exists_nonempty(p):
            continue
        unit, day, suffix = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), m.group(3)
        out.setdefault((unit, day), []).append((suffix, p))
    for items in out.values():
        items.sort(key=lambda t: (t[0] is not None, t[0] or ""))
    return out


lessons = collect("lessons", "lesson", "qmd")
preps = collect("preps", "prep", "qmd")
slides = collect("lecture_slides", "slide", "qmd")
notebooks = collect("notebooks", "notebook", "ipynb")
practice = collect("practice", "practice", "qmd")
for key, items in collect("practice", "practice", "ipynb").items():
    practice.setdefault(key, []).extend(items)
for items in practice.values():
    items.sort(key=lambda t: (t[0] is not None, t[0] or ""))

row_keys = sorted(set(lessons) | set(preps) | set(slides) | set(notebooks) | set(practice))


def mwf_dates(start: date, count: int):
    d, out = start, []
    while len(out) < count:
        if d.weekday() in (0, 2, 4):  # Mon, Wed, Fri
            out.append(d)
        d += timedelta(days=1)
    return out


today = date.today()
computed_dates = mwf_dates(FIRST_MEETING, len(row_keys))
future_idx = next((i for i, dd in enumerate(computed_dates) if dd > today), None)


def date_cell(i: int, d: date) -> str:
    if d <= today or i == future_idx:
        return f"{d.strftime('%b')} {d.day}, {d.year}"
    return "TBD"


def label_for(emoji: str, suffix, noun: str) -> str:
    if suffix is None:
        return emoji
    extra = suffix.replace("_", " ").replace("-", " ").title()
    return f"{emoji} {html.escape(extra)}"


def local_link_cell(items, emoji: str, noun: str, html_dir: str) -> str:
    if not items:
        return ""
    cells = []
    for suffix, path in items:
        href = f"{html_dir}/{path.stem}.html"
        title_attr = "" if suffix is None else f' title="{html.escape(noun)}: {html.escape(suffix)}"'
        cells.append(f'<a href="{html.escape(href)}"{title_attr}>{label_for(emoji, suffix, noun)}</a>')
    return " ".join(cells)


def notebook_link_cell(items) -> str:
    if not items:
        return ""
    cells = []
    for suffix, path in items:
        label = label_for(NOTEBOOK_EMOJI, suffix, "Notebook")
        if NOTEBOOK_BASE:
            tail = path.stem[len("notebook"):]  # e.g. "1_1" or "1_1_example"
            href = f"{NOTEBOOK_BASE}{tail}.ipynb"
            cells.append(
                f'<a href="{html.escape(href)}" title="{html.escape(NOTEBOOK_HOVER)}" target="_blank">'
                f"{label}</a>"
            )
        else:
            cells.append(label)
    return " ".join(cells)


def unit_label(u: int) -> str:
    p = Path("lessons") / f"unit{u}.qmd"
    if exists_nonempty(p):
        return f'<a href="lessons/unit{u}.html">Unit {u}</a>'
    return f"Unit {u}"


rows = []
for (u, d) in row_keys:
    lesson_items = lessons.get((u, d), [])
    if lesson_items:
        _, lesson_path = lesson_items[0]
        topic_cell = html.escape(get_title(lesson_path, f"Day {u}.{d}"))
        lesson_cell = f'<a href="lessons/{lesson_path.stem}.html" title="Lesson">{LESSON_EMOJI}</a>'
    else:
        topic_cell = f"Day {u}.{d}"
        lesson_cell = ""

    rows.append({
        "unit": u,
        "topic": topic_cell,
        "lesson": lesson_cell,
        "prep": local_link_cell(preps.get((u, d), []), PREP_EMOJI, "Prep", "preps"),
        "slides": local_link_cell(slides.get((u, d), []), SLIDES_EMOJI, "Slides", "lecture_slides"),
        "notebook": notebook_link_cell(notebooks.get((u, d), [])),
        "practice": local_link_cell(practice.get((u, d), []), PRACTICE_EMOJI, "Practice", "practice"),
    })

for i, r in enumerate(rows):
    r["date"] = date_cell(i, computed_dates[i])

if not rows:
    print("_No lessons published yet — check back soon._")
else:
    body = []
    i, n = 0, len(rows)
    while i < n:
        u = rows[i]["unit"]
        span = 1
        while i + span < n and rows[i + span]["unit"] == u:
            span += 1
        unit_html = unit_label(u)
        for j in range(span):
            r = rows[i + j]
            unit_td = f'<td rowspan="{span}">{unit_html}</td>' if j == 0 else ""
            body.append(
                f'<tr>{unit_td}<td>{r["date"]}</td><td>{r["topic"]}</td><td>{r["lesson"]}</td>'
                f'<td>{r["prep"]}</td><td>{r["slides"]}</td>'
                f'<td>{r["notebook"]}</td><td>{r["practice"]}</td></tr>'
            )
        i += span

    table = [
        '<table class="schedule">',
        "<thead><tr><th>Unit</th><th>Date</th><th>Topic</th><th>Lesson</th>"
        "<th>Prep</th><th>Slides</th><th>Notebooks</th><th>Practice</th></tr></thead>",
        "<tbody>",
        *body,
        "</tbody>",
        "</table>",
    ]
    print("\n".join(table))
```

# Course Objectives

- Build AI agent harnesses
- Evaluate agents using agent observability tools
- Translate ambiguous production goals into explicit architectural decisions and measurable success criteria
- Communicate about AI using language fitted to the audience
- Use quality sources to self-learn in an ever-changing AI landscape
- Form and live a personal ethic for the use of AI agents

## Unit 2
### Diagnostics — Why Is It "Bad"? (Weeks 5–8)


**Goal:** Develop diagnostic tools to peer into the black box of agentic AI, in preparation for building reliable agents.

**Topics:**
- Categories of agent failure: errors, loops, cost explosion, hallucination, unreliability
- Observability and tracing with LangSmith
- Token and latency analysis
- Debugging hallucinations and unexpected behavior
- Prompt failure patterns
- Cost and loop failure analysis
- Identifying and fixing code bugs

**Project:** Diagnostic Report — Fix a Broken Agent

You are given a pre-built broken agent to diagnose. Your job is to implement tracing, identify every failure, document root causes, and produce a structured diagnostic report. You will implement at least one fix and verify it with traces before presenting to the class.

**Outcomes:**
- Set up LangSmith and capture screenshot traces
- Implement tracing features and explain what each one does and why
- Measure token usage and latency across tool calls and LLM responses
- Identify categories of agent failure from trace data
- Distinguish model errors from prompt errors from code bugs
- Identify and rewrite failing prompts based on traced results
- Implement basic loop guards and context limits
- Fix identified bugs and verify with re-tracing
- Produce and present a diagnostic report

**Note on AI use:** AI assistance may be permitted this unit — details TBD. If used, post in Slack what you discussed and any lessons learned.

**Daily Schedule:**

| Day | Topic |
|-----|-------|
| 1 | What Makes an Agent "Bad"? — review Unit 1 failures, intro observability, define runs/traces, navigate LangSmith |
| 2 | Defining Main Failures — define failure types, compare good vs bad traces |
| 3 | LangSmith Setup & Trace Reading — get API key, set up tracing, interpret each step of a trace |
| 4 | Token & Latency Analysis — monitor performance, choose evaluation metrics, understand cost growth |
| 5 | Evals & Golden Test Sets — build a test set, write success criteria, judge outputs |
| 6 | Debugging Failure Patterns — repeatable diagnostic process, categorize and prioritize failures |
| 7 | Automation Rules & Alerts — sampling, filters, and alerts to catch bad runs; connect user feedback to trace evidence |
| 8 | Diagnosing a Broken Agent — provide a diagnostic report, apply a fix, retest and compare |
| 9 | Unit Review & Assessment — unit review and decided testing method |
| Project | Diagnostic Report — trace, document, and fix a pre-built broken agent; present findings to the class |

## Unit 3
### Context Engineering — Make a "Good" Agent (Weeks 9–12)


> **⚠️ Unit 3 is currently in production.** Days will be added as they are finalized.

**Goal:** Engineer context effectively to produce agents that are reliable, specialized, and capable of operating over long horizons — then prove it in competition.

**Topics:**
- Context engineering vs. prompt engineering
- The 4 levels of intent: session, user, organization, world
- Simple context management: truncation, summarization, selection, file write, database, isolation/delegation
- Context offloading: semantic search, forgetting vector, graph memory
- Subagent architecture: parallelization, serialization, concurrency
- Checkpointing, human-in-the-loop, and context self-adaptation
- Grounding and RAG
- Long-horizon task planning
- Cost-aware context design

**Project:** Battle of the Bots

Apply everything from all three units to build a production-ready agent of your own design. Agents compete in structured challenges testing usefulness, resilience, and cost efficiency. The best agent is not necessarily the most powerful — it is the most reliable, the most purposeful, and the most improved from where you started in Unit 1.

**Outcomes:**
- Define context engineering and distinguish it from prompt engineering
- Implement truncation and summarization-based context management
- Apply context offloading using semantic search or graph memory
- Implement parallelized and serialized subagent patterns
- Add checkpointing and human-in-the-loop interrupts
- Build a RAG pipeline and test retrieval quality
- Design agents that maintain state across long multi-step tasks
- Apply context engineering improvements to the Unit 1 personal assistant
- Compete in Battle of the Bots and articulate design decisions made

**Note on AI use:** AI assistance may be permitted this unit — details TBD. If used, post in Slack what you discussed and any lessons learned.

**Daily Schedule:**

| Day | Topic |
|-----|-------|
| 1 | What Is Context Engineering? — definition, levels of intent, why prompting alone isn't enough |
| 2 | Planning Agentic Systems — distinguish prompt, context, and intent engineering; plan systems on a whiteboard |
| 3 | Context Management Strategies — truncate, summarize, select, file write, database, isolate/delegate; implement all three core types |
| *More days coming* | *Check back as Unit 3 is finalized* |
